claims.title: Stefan Nemanja founds the Nemanjić state
claims.summary: As grand chieftain of Raška, Stefan Nemanja united the Serb principalities and founded the Nemanjić dynasty, which would develop Serbia into a major medieval Balkan power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1166-stefan-nemanja-founds-the-nemanjic-state, claim TL:SRB:event:1166:stefan-nemanja-founds-the-nemanjic-state, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Foundation of Studenica Monastery
claims.summary: Stefan Nemanja founded the marble monastery of Studenica, retiring there around 1196; its churches became a masterpiece of the Raška school and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1190-foundation-of-studenica-monastery, claim TL:SRB:event:1190:foundation-of-studenica-monastery, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Stefan the First-Crowned becomes king
claims.summary: Stefan Nemanjić obtained recognition as king, raising the grand principality of Raška to the rank of a kingdom and earning the name Prvovenčani, the 'First-Crowned'.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1217-stefan-the-first-crowned-becomes-king, claim TL:SRB:event:1217:stefan-the-first-crowned-becomes-king, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Autocephaly of the Serbian Orthodox Church
claims.summary: Saint Sava obtained from the patriarch at Nicaea the status of autocephalous archbishop, founding an independent Serbian church that bound religious and royal authority together.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1219-autocephaly-of-the-serbian-orthodox-church, claim TL:SRB:event:1219:autocephaly-of-the-serbian-orthodox-church, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Imperial coronation of Stefan Dušan
claims.summary: Having expanded the realm across the southern Balkans, Stefan Dušan was crowned 'Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks' and raised the church of Peć to a patriarchate, the high point of medieval Serbia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1346-imperial-coronation-of-stefan-dusan, claim TL:SRB:event:1346:imperial-coronation-of-stefan-dusan, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Death of Dušan and the empire's collapse
claims.summary: The death of Stefan Dušan in 1355 led to the rapid disintegration of the Serbian Empire into rival principalities, leaving the Balkans divided as the Ottomans advanced.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1355-death-of-dusan-and-the-empire-s-collapse, claim TL:SRB:event:1355:death-of-dusan-and-the-empire-s-collapse, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Battle of Kosovo
claims.summary: On the Field of Blackbirds the army of Prince Lazar fought the Ottoman sultan Murad I; both leaders were killed and Serbian resistance was broken, making Kosovo the central event of national memory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1389-the-battle-of-kosovo, claim TL:SRB:event:1389:the-battle-of-kosovo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Serbian Despotate
claims.summary: A reduced Serbian state survived as the Despotate, ruled latterly from Smederevo and balancing between the Ottomans and Hungary, prolonging Serb statehood for another half-century.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1402-the-serbian-despotate, claim TL:SRB:event:1402:the-serbian-despotate, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ottoman conquest of Serbia
claims.summary: The Ottomans captured the fortress of Smederevo and extinguished the Despotate, absorbing the Serb lands into the empire and beginning nearly four centuries of Ottoman rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1459-ottoman-conquest-of-serbia, claim TL:SRB:event:1459:ottoman-conquest-of-serbia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Patriarchate of Peć
claims.summary: Elevated under Dušan, the patriarchate of Peć became the spiritual heart of the Serbs; its medieval churches in Kosovo survive as UNESCO World Heritage monuments of the Serbian Orthodox tradition.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1346-patriarchate-of-pec, claim TL:SRB:event:1346:patriarchate-of-pec, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Serbian Uprising
claims.summary: Led by Karađorđe, Serbs rose against Ottoman rule and for nearly a decade governed a self-proclaimed state, the opening act of the Serbian Revolution before its suppression in 1813.

sources.label: Serbia: The disintegration of Ottoman rule

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1804-first-serbian-uprising, claim TL:SRB:event:1804:first-serbian-uprising, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Uprising and autonomy under Miloš Obrenović
claims.summary: Miloš Obrenović led the Second Uprising; by 1830 the Ottomans granted the principality full autonomy under him as hereditary prince, establishing self-governing Serbia.

sources.label: Serbia: The disintegration of Ottoman rule

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1815-second-uprising-and-autonomy-under-milos, claim TL:SRB:event:1815:second-uprising-and-autonomy-under-milos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence recognised at the Congress of Berlin
claims.summary: The Treaty of Berlin confirmed Serbia's full independence in international law and enlarged the principality, which became the Kingdom of Serbia in 1882.

sources.label: Serbia: The disintegration of Ottoman rule
A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations, by Country: Serbia
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1878-independence-recognised-at-the-congress-of, claim TL:SRB:event:1878:independence-recognised-at-the-congress-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Balkan Wars
claims.summary: Serbia drove the Ottomans from most of their European lands and, after the Second Balkan War, gained Kosovo, Metohija and much of Macedonia, nearly doubling its territory and alarming Austria-Hungary.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1912-the-balkan-wars, claim TL:SRB:event:1912:the-balkan-wars, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination at Sarajevo
claims.summary: The Bosnian Serb Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo; Austria-Hungary blamed Serbia, and its declaration of war triggered the First World War.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1914-assassination-at-sarajevo, claim TL:SRB:event:1914:assassination-at-sarajevo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes proclaimed
claims.summary: Prince Regent Alexander proclaimed the South Slav kingdom in Belgrade, uniting Serbia and Montenegro with former Habsburg lands under the Serbian crown; it was renamed Yugoslavia in 1929.

sources.label: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1918-kingdom-of-serbs-croats-and-slovenes-proclaimed, claim TL:SRB:event:1918:kingdom-of-serbs-croats-and-slovenes-proclaimed, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Royal dictatorship and renaming as Yugoslavia
claims.summary: Amid party deadlock King Alexander suspended the constitution, imposed a royal dictatorship and renamed the state the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, deepening tensions among its nations.

sources.label: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1929-royal-dictatorship-and-renaming-as-yugoslavia, claim TL:SRB:event:1929:royal-dictatorship-and-renaming-as-yugoslavia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Axis invasion and occupation
claims.summary: Germany and its allies invaded and dismembered Yugoslavia in April 1941, placing Serbia under occupation and unleashing a multi-sided war of resistance and civil conflict.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1941-axis-invasion-and-occupation, claim TL:SRB:event:1941:axis-invasion-and-occupation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Socialist Yugoslavia under Tito
claims.summary: Tito's Partisans triumphed and built a socialist federation of six republics; after breaking with Stalin in 1948, Yugoslavia pursued non-alignment, with Serbia its largest republic.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1945-socialist-yugoslavia-under-tito, claim TL:SRB:event:1945:socialist-yugoslavia-under-tito, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Autonomy for Vojvodina and Kosovo
claims.summary: The federal constitution of 1974 granted wide autonomy to the Serbian provinces of Vojvodina and Kosovo, a settlement resented by many Serbs that would ignite conflict after Tito's death.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1974-autonomy-for-vojvodina-and-kosovo, claim TL:SRB:event:1974:autonomy-for-vojvodina-and-kosovo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Milošević curtails Kosovo's autonomy
claims.summary: Riding a wave of Serbian nationalism, Slobodan Milošević revoked the autonomy of Kosovo and Vojvodina, deepening the crisis that would break Yugoslavia apart.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1989-milosevic-curtails-kosovo-s-autonomy, claim TL:SRB:event:1989:milosevic-curtails-kosovo-s-autonomy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Wars in Croatia and Bosnia
claims.summary: As Yugoslavia disintegrated, war engulfed Croatia and Bosnia amid ethnic cleansing and atrocity, with Belgrade backing Serb forces and the federation collapsing into a rump Yugoslavia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1991-wars-in-croatia-and-bosnia, claim TL:SRB:event:1991:wars-in-croatia-and-bosnia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kosovo War and NATO bombing
claims.summary: After fighting between Yugoslav forces and the Kosovo Liberation Army and the displacement of Albanian civilians, NATO bombed Yugoslavia for some eleven weeks until Milošević agreed to withdraw from Kosovo.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1999-kosovo-war-and-nato-bombing, claim TL:SRB:event:1999:kosovo-war-and-nato-bombing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: UN Security Council Resolution 1244
claims.summary: The Security Council placed Kosovo under an international civil (UNMIK) and security presence, granting substantial autonomy while reaffirming the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Yugoslavia.

sources.label: United Nations Security Council Resolution 1244 (1999)
sources.publisher: United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-1999-un-security-council-resolution-1244, claim TL:SRB:event:1999:un-security-council-resolution-1244, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Milošević
claims.summary: After disputed elections, mass protests in Belgrade forced Milošević from power; he was later tried at the ICTY in The Hague but died in 2006 before a verdict was reached.

sources.label: Slobodan Milošević (IT-02-54) case information
sources.publisher: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (UN-IRMCT)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-2000-fall-of-milosevic, claim TL:SRB:event:2000:fall-of-milosevic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Montenegro's independence and the end of the State Union
claims.summary: Following a referendum on 21 May 2006, Montenegro declared independence; Serbia accepted the result and declared itself the successor state, dissolving the State Union of Serbia and Montenegro.

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition, Diplomatic, and Consular Relations, by Country: Serbia
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-2006-montenegro-s-independence-and-the-end-of-the, claim TL:SRB:event:2006:montenegro-s-independence-and-the-end-of-the, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kosovo declares independence
claims.summary: Kosovo's assembly declared independence from Serbia, a step recognised by many Western states but rejected by Serbia, which continues to regard Kosovo as its autonomous province.

sources.label: Accordance with international law of the unilateral declaration of independence in respect of Kosovo — Advisory Opinion of 22 July 2010

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-2008-kosovo-declares-independence, claim TL:SRB:event:2008:kosovo-declares-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: ICJ advisory opinion on Kosovo
claims.summary: The International Court of Justice found that Kosovo's 2008 declaration of independence did not violate international law; Serbia continued nonetheless to withhold recognition.

sources.label: Accordance with international law of the unilateral declaration of independence in respect of Kosovo — Advisory Opinion of 22 July 2010

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-2010-icj-advisory-opinion-on-kosovo, claim TL:SRB:event:2010:icj-advisory-opinion-on-kosovo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Brussels Agreement
claims.summary: In the EU-facilitated dialogue, Belgrade and Pristina reached the First Agreement of Principles, integrating Serb-majority northern Kosovo into Kosovo's institutions without constituting Serbian recognition.

sources.label: Belgrade–Pristina Dialogue: Agreement on the path to normalisation between Kosovo and Serbia

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Serbia: From the medieval Nemanjić kingdom and the field of Kosovo to a modern Balkan republic at the centre of Europe's last great territorial dispute.", terralore.co/country/SRB/chronicle#ev-2013-brussels-agreement, claim TL:SRB:event:2013:brussels-agreement, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Agreement on the Path to Normalisation (Ohrid)
claims.summary: Serbia and Kosovo agreed to develop normal relations and recognise each other's documents and symbols, with an implementation annex agreed at Ohrid, while leaving the question of status unresolved.

sources.label: Belgrade–Pristina Dialogue: Agreement on the path to normalisation between Kosovo and Serbia
